hood_desc: The practical provincial capital with the night market, riverside walkway, and long-distance transport hub, less touristy than the beach areas.
The area's main beach resort strip, packed with hotels, dive shops, and restaurants, and the jumping-off point for island boat tours.
A stunning cliff-backed peninsula reachable only by boat, world-famous for rock climbing and its beach bars.

A quiet resort beach about a 20-minute drive northwest of Ao Nang, with low-rise beachfront hotels, a few restaurants and massage shops, and none of the strip nightlife. It suits families and couples who want a calm base within easy reach of the Ao Nang boat piers.

food.name: Gaeng Som Pla
food.desc: Southern sour orange curry: fish simmered in a thin, fiercely hot turmeric and tamarind broth. Sour and spicy with no coconut milk to soften it.

places.name: Ruen Mai
places.note: Widely called the best southern Thai kitchen in Krabi; leafy garden setting, no view needed.

places.name: Potjawan
places.note: Seafood-heavy local menu with a proper gaeng som pla and raw prawns in fish sauce.

places.name: Baitoey Seafood Restaurant
places.note: Authentic southern cooking with river views; calmer than the Ao Nang strip.

food.name: Fresh Grilled Seafood
food.desc: Whole snapper, saltwater crab, tiger prawns, scallops and squid, picked live from the tanks and grilled or fried with garlic and pepper.

places.name: Krua Thara
places.note: Locals' choice for genuinely fresh fish at fair prices; tanks of swimming seafood out front.

places.name: Lae Lay Grill
places.note: Clifftop tables with sweeping bay views; come for sunset and book ahead.

places.name: Baitoey Seafood Restaurant
places.note: Long-running riverside seafood house, better value than the beach restaurants.

food.name: Gaeng Tai Pla
food.desc: The hardest-core southern curry: fermented fish innards cooked down with turmeric, chili and bamboo shoots. Pungent, salty and seriously hot.

places.name: Ruen Mai
places.note: Cooks the full southern repertoire, including dishes tourist kitchens leave off the menu.

places.name: Krabi Town curry shophouses
places.note: Point-and-choose curry counters where tai pla sits in the trays at lunchtime.

food.name: Pad Bai Liang
food.desc: Bai liang, a nutty southern jungle green, stir-fried fast with egg and garlic. Simple, cheap, and the vegetable dish that balances all those curries.

places.name: Ruen Mai
places.note: Serves a wide range of local greens; bai liang with egg is a house staple.

places.name: Krua Thara
places.note: Good order to balance a table of grilled seafood; arrives fast and costs very little.

food.name: Khanom Jeen
food.desc: Fermented rice vermicelli ladled with your choice of curry and piled with free raw vegetables, pickles and herbs. The classic southern Thai breakfast.

places.name: Maharaj Road khanom jeen shop
places.area: West side of Maharaj Road, Krabi Town
places.note: Popular with locals, rarely found by visitors; pick your curry at the counter, greens are free.

places.name: Chao Fah Night Market
places.note: Evening stalls sell it alongside other southern staples; open daily from around 5pm.

food.name: Roti and Massaman
food.desc: Krabi's Thai-Muslim side: flaky griddled roti eaten with massaman curry or condensed milk and banana, plus grilled chicken and spiced rice soups.

places.name: Chao Fah Night Market
places.area: In front of Chao Fah Park, Krabi Town
places.note: Riverfront market with roti carts, English menus and plenty of seating, 5pm to 10pm daily.

places.name: Walking Street Night Market
places.note: Friday to Sunday evenings, a much bigger spread of stalls plus a performance stage.

places.name: Ao Nang Boat Noodle and Thai Food
places.note: Cheap, well-reviewed local kitchen for noodles and curries, walking distance from the beach.

food.name: Cha Yen
food.desc: Thai iced tea: strong orange-tinged black tea sweetened with condensed and evaporated milk over crushed ice. Sold everywhere for pocket change.

places.name: Chao Fah Night Market
places.note: Drink carts throughout the market; ask for wan noi if you want it less sweet.

places.name: Ao Nang beach road cafes
places.note: Every cafe on the strip pours it; also try cha manao, the lime version, in the heat.

food.name: Fresh Coconut Water
food.desc: A chilled young coconut hacked open at the top, drunk through a straw and then scraped out for the soft jelly flesh inside.

places.name: Ao Nang beachfront vendors
places.note: Carts along the sand sell them chilled; cheapest a few streets back from the beach.

places.name: Krua Thara
places.note: Served alongside the seafood; a good non-alcoholic partner to a fiery southern curry.

landmarks: Accessible only by longtail boat, this peninsula of white sand and soaring karst cliffs is a world mecca for rock climbers and beach dreamers.
Beneath a cliff shrine dedicated to a sea princess, this ranks among Asia's most beautiful beaches, framed by stalactites and jade water.
A punishing 1,260-step climb ascends to a golden Buddha and giddying 360-degree panorama over karst towers and the Andaman coast.
Four Islands Tour (Ko Poda, Chicken Island, Ko Tup, Ko Mor)
Longtails hop between postcard islets linked by a tidal sandbar, delivering the classic snorkelling-and-swimming sampler of Krabi's seascape.
A hidden emerald lagoon opens inside this ringed limestone island, with a 360-degree viewpoint tower and powder beaches nearby.
Krabi's lively resort strip lines a cliff-flanked bay of longtail boats, the springboard for island tours, sunset dinners and massage shacks.
Twin 100-metre limestone peaks flanking the Krabi River guard the town like gateposts, with caves of stalactites and prehistoric traces to explore.
Krabi Town Riverfront and Night Market
Giant mud-crab sculptures and karst views line the promenade, while the weekend walking street serves Krabi's best street food and souvenirs.

train.note: Krabi has no railway. The nearest station is Trang, about two hours away by road, or Surat Thani about three and a half, both on the State Railway of Thailand southern line (https://www.dticket.railway.co.th/) with sleepers to Bangkok. Most visitors fly into Krabi airport or arrive by bus.

bus.note: The Malaysia coaches are sold as through tickets but usually involve a change in Hat Yai and a border stop at Sadao - allow a full day. Domestic buses from the Krabi bus terminal at Talat Kao run to Bangkok overnight (about 12 hours), Phuket (3) and Surat Thani (3), on Transport Co. (https://www.transport.co.th/) and private operators; book through 12Go.

ferry.note: There are no international sailings from Krabi. The Phi Phi boats run year-round from Klong Jilad pier a few kilometres from town, but many of the smaller island routes operate only in the November-April dry season and stop in the monsoon. Railay has no road at all, so the longtail from Ao Nang is the only way in. Boats are cancelled in rough seas, which is common from May to October.

half.name: Ao Thalane Mangrove Kayaking
half.blurb: A mangrove estuary a short drive from Krabi town where kayak tours pass limestone karsts, tidal caves, and quiet channels lined with mangrove roots.

half.name: Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot)
half.blurb: A jungle boardwalk leads to this luminous natural spring pool, its glassy green water welling from thermal streams in Thung Teao forest.

half.name: Klong Thom Hot Springs Waterfall
half.blurb: Warm mineral water cascades over smooth travertine tiers into natural jungle jacuzzis, the perfect pairing with the nearby Emerald Pool.

full.name: Phi Phi Islands
full.blurb: An island group reached by speedboat in about 90 minutes from Krabi, with Maya Bay's cliffs and Ko Phi Phi Don's viewpoints and beaches.

full.name: Phang Nga Bay
full.blurb: A limestone-studded bay north of Krabi featuring the karst tower known from James Bond films, reached by longtail boat from Surakul Pier.

notes.walk: Krabi Town's riverside and night market are walkable; Railay, Ao Nang, and the islands require a longtail boat, songthaew, or organized tour
notes.card: Accepted at larger hotels and restaurants; cash preferred at markets and beach vendors
notes.safety: Generally safe and tourism-oriented; standard beach and boat-safety precautions apply. Petty theft on crowded beaches and overcharging by unlicensed boat operators are the main concerns.
notes.religion: Buddhism (majority); Islam (significant minority, especially in southern Thailand)
notes.langs: Thai; English (widely spoken in tourist areas)
notes.net: Good 4G coverage in town and Ao Nang, patchier on remote islands. Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes. ~$5-12 for a 10-15GB prepaid tourist SIM. Free wifi widely available. An AIS or DTAC tourist SIM or eSIM.
notes.transit: Songthaews (shared pickup trucks) around Krabi Town and to Ao Nang; longtail boats to Railay and the islands
notes.transport: Krabi International Airport (KBV), about 20 min from Krabi Town. No passenger rail service to Krabi. Long-distance buses connect to Bangkok (about 12 hr), Phuket, and Surat Thani. Ferries connect Krabi to Phi Phi Islands, Koh Lanta, and Phuket. Rental cars and scooters available; roads connect Krabi Town and Ao Nang directly.
